s0401.literal: Your servant formerly repeatedly saw Household Superintendent Pei Quan apply mind earnest-sincere; Gentleman-in-Attendance Qin Ji several times ascended memorial-openings remonstrating;
s0401.idiomatic: I have often watched Crown Prince Household Superintendent Pei Quan serve with wrenching earnestness and Gentleman Qin Ji memorial after memorial beseech the throne.

s0402.literal: yet Yuan Qian posthumously gifted with Nine Columns; Quan had loyal intent, alone did not receive reward.
s0402.idiomatic: Yet Yuan Qian won posthumous honours among the Nine Ministers while Pei Quan, though loyal as any of them, received nothing.

s0403.literal: say ought accord Qian as precedent, thereby grace his shade.
s0403.idiomatic: Treat Pei Quan by the same measure granted Yuan Qian and let his ghost know favour.

s0404.literal: Tracing-search memorial-tablets—such as Qin Ji's sort and Metropolitan Shepherd memorialized—all those daring bow resign along roads—bright edict praised-displayed them, causing faint difference from masses—thereby encourage doing good—thereby reward future also.
s0404.idiomatic: Survey the petitions—Qin Ji's and the Metropolitan Shepherd's—praising men who dared surrender their seals in the highroad dust; your luminous edict singled them out so virtue would spread and posterity take heart.

s0406.literal: Now Chancellor of State although already Tutor-Protector Eastern Palace, safeguards its peace-peril.
s0406.idiomatic: The Chancellor of State is already grand and junior tutor—he guards the heir's life and death.

s0407.literal: Reaching dawn-evening instruction-lecture, assistant-guide exit-enter, movement-still toil-labour—ought select cold-bitter knights, loyal pure upright, old yet not failing—such as Gates Colonel Liang Liu, white-clothes Nan'an Zhu Chong's like—thereby make Tutor-Protector.
s0407.idiomatic: For the daily coaching, the comings and goings, the bone-wearying round of duty, pick men of chilly gates and proven honor—men like Gates Colonel Liang Liu or the hemp-robed recluse Zhu Chong of Nan'an—and set them over him as tutors.

s0408.literal: Those serving ministers below civil-martial generals clerks—forthwith again not take flourishing-kins great-gate sons-younger—such as Consort Wu's house-relations and Jia, Guo factions.
s0408.idiomatic: Do not staff his attendants and guards from the riot of princely in-laws—no more of Consort Wu's clan or the Jia and Guo packs.

s0409.literal: Such ilk—born then wealth-overflow; no thought cultivate self; norm many light-thin float-flower; mutually urge unrestraint—all not that which benefits our young lord.
s0409.idiomatic: Men soaked in gold from the cradle never trouble to temper themselves; they glide through life on perfume and dare—none of them strengthens a boy who must wear the crown.

s0410.literal: All can select cold-gate pure-conduct, learning question plain knights, repeated walked peril-easy, integrity righteousness sufficient praised—thereby equip crowd ministers—can lighten their ritual-etiquette—cause with antiquity same—thereby mutually polish-cut as benefit.
s0410.idiomatic: Fill the household instead with poor gate scholars of tested fiber, men who have ridden fortune's switchbacks and earned a name for constancy; relax the court drill so they may speak as elders did and sharpen one another like whetstones.

s0411.literal: Anciently Wei Wendi in Eastern Palace—Xu Gan, Liu Zhen as friends—literary learning connect-receive Way together like breath-kind.
s0411.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Wei was heir, Xu Gan and Liu Zhen were his companions; their brush and book traffic breathed the same air as his own.

s0412.literal: Wu Heir Deng—Gu Tan as friend, Zhuge Ke as guest—slept same bed-curtain, walking then three-horse chariot—association like plain cloth—mutual call by style—this then near-generation bright parallel.
s0412.idiomatic: Crown Prince Deng of Wu kept Gu Tan as friend and Zhuge Ke as mentor; they shared a couch, rode the second chariot at his side, called one another by courtesy name like village neighbors—a mirror for our own age.

s0413.literal: Son-of-Heaven's sons not worry not wealth-noble; not worry people not fear-revere—worry lies in pride-overflow, not hear one's fault, not know grain-agriculture's hardship difficulty ear.
s0413.idiomatic: A Son of Heaven's boy need not fear poverty or want of awe; he must dread arrogance, deafness to blame, and ignorance of what the plough costs.

s0414.literal: Reaching extreme ones—then not know names six domestic beasts—can not strive!
s0414.idiomatic: Worst of all are heirs who cannot tell ox from horse—can we afford not to drill them?

s0415.literal: Anciently Duke Zhou personally whipped Bo Qin; Cao Can bamboo-thrashed Jiao two hundred—sagely fathers kind fathers all not harmed grace.
s0415.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou flogged Bo Qin; Cao Can caned his son Cao Jiao two hundred strokes—holy fathers broke skin without breaking love.

s0416.literal: Now not bear small mutual indulgent-sustain—order reach fault-miss suddenly mutually blame-punish—not also error!
s0416.idiomatic: If you cannot bear a tutor's small discipline now, you will only watch the boy fail and flay his keepers later—what folly is that?

s0417.literal: Within rites crown prince dawn-dusk inspects meals—dusk-fix dawn-inquire—kneel ask peace-fouling—at feeling obtains exhaust.
s0417.idiomatic: Ritual sets the heir beside his father's tray morning and night, evening his rest and dawn his health, kneeling to ask after him until duty is spent.

s0418.literal: Five-days one court-audience—in respect already simple; in grace also distant—easy bring about frame-between.
s0418.idiomatic: An audience every five days slights filial punctilio and thins affection—an open door for slander between you.

s0419.literal: Therefore it is said, 'If one morning he does not attend, a knife can slip into the gap.'
s0419.idiomatic: The adage runs, 'Miss a single morning audience and a blade can slide into the breach.'

s0420.literal: Five-days regulation—rose Han Gaozu—himself was Son of Heaven—father was commoner—myriad pivot affairs many—therefore lacked private reverence ear.
s0420.idiomatic: The five-day rule began with Han Gaozu, Son of Heaven whose father was still a common busyman and whose desk overflowed—so private courtesy gave way.

s0421.literal: Now Sovereign above holds court—crown prince without affairs—solely oversees filial nurture—ought alter this vulgar custom.
s0421.idiomatic: Today the emperor governs alone while the heir has no war to fight; nothing should stop him honoring a father daily—discard that Han habit.

s0422.literal: The chapter 'Royal Heir of King Wen' says: 'When Wang Ji took one meal he took one meal; when he took two meals he took two meals.
s0422.idiomatic: The Documents of Ritual recall King Wen's heir: Wang Ji lifted his bowl once and the prince matched him; Wang Ji lifted it twice and the prince matched again.

s0423.idiomatic: Who under heaven excuses lounging toward a father's kitchen with audiences only every fifth dawn?

s0425.literal: Now welcoming crown prince spirit-casket—solitary shade sole travels—imperial great-grandson tender-dash—cannot ford roads.
s0425.idiomatic: The crown prince's catafalque is coming home unattended, while the imperial great-grandson is too young for the bitter road east.

s0426.literal: Say can dispatch Consort undertake welcome far road—order her father Yang Yan accompany travel guard-protect.
s0426.idiomatic: Send his consort to meet the cortège on the distant road and set her father Yang Yan at her side as escort.

s0427.literal: When imperial heir first sight slandered-framed—Your servant household-gate lacked blessing—three generations sham-kin—all tasted bitterness—take house observe state—firmly knew crown prince had change-disaster.
s0427.idiomatic: When they first framed the heir, my house—three generations joined to the throne by paper marriages—had no luck and knew every grief; what our kin suffered told me the palace would turn on him.

s0428.literal: Your servant therefore sought vice Supervisor-of-State—wished rely on Bing Ji's old precedent—ward off resist coming envoys—supply-nurture embrace-guard—body personally drink-food medicine—hope sufficient rescue peril.
s0428.idiomatic: So I begged to serve as vice overseer of the realm, to replay Bing Ji's old trick of barring false couriers, to feed and shield the boy with my own hands and physic—anything to snatch him from ruin.

s0429.literal: Responsible officials because Your servant name standing light shallow—unwilling grant see give.
s0429.idiomatic: The bureaus refused: my name was too slight for such trust.

s0430.literal: Age's people seeing laugh—say for this post advance-retreat hard dwell—have certain-death worry.
s0430.idiomatic: The world sneered that the post was a trap—advance or retreat, you died.

s0431.literal: Your servant alone deemed if preserve heir-apparent—even Jia clan execute—sweet-heart wished desire.
s0431.idiomatic: I alone reckoned that saving the storied heir—even at the price of every Jia head—would be joy enough.

s0432.literal: Now regency supervising censors and their direct aides all slated Three-Clans extinction—retinue guards remiss—in truth rightly thus.
s0432.idiomatic: Now the inspectors and aides who guarded the regency heir stand sentenced to three-generation extinction—the household guard rightly shares the scaffold on paper.

s0433.literal: Your servant deem them petty men—not worth fully blame.
s0433.idiomatic: Yet they were frightened little men—not worth exhausting your wrath upon.

s0434.literal: Therefore Confucius said: 'He may be entrusted with a six-foot orphan; confronted with great crisis he cannot be wrested.
s0434.idiomatic: Hence the Master's words: Charge him with a boy in mourning; drive him toward the breaking wave—and he cannot be peeled from integrity.

s0435.idiomatic: That is why sage-kings sift appointments as if their lives hung on them.

s0436.literal: Therefore Henan Intendant Xiang Xiong—anciently able violate-difficulty bury former general Zhong Hui—Wendi praised him—first pulled manifest employ—reaching former emperor—made him Right Lead.
s0436.idiomatic: Consider Xiang Xiong of Henan, who braved edict to bury his old commander Zhong Hui; Emperor Wen exalted him, pulled him from obscurity, and the late emperor named him right-side guide to the heir.

s0437.literal: If touching recent affairs—if obtain Xiong's likeness—then how could be harmed!
s0437.idiomatic: Had the latest summons found a conscience like Xiang Xiong's clasped to the boy, what hand could harm him?

s0438.literal: These two envoys—only were foolish cowardly—also not join plot—only can execute body—self preserve Three Clans.
s0438.idiomatic: The two couriers were craven dolts, not plotters—behead them if you must, but spare their kin.

s0439.literal: As for Guo Xu, Guo Bin—then as to punishment as appropriate.
s0439.idiomatic: Guo Xu and Guo Bin are another matter—here the blade fits.

s0440.literal: Further Eastern Palace also ought wonder-select loyal straight bright upright—such as Xiong's comparison.
s0440.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace itself needs men as straight as Xiang Xiong.

s0441.literal: When Your Majesty thousand autumns myriad years after—imperial great-grandson tender-dash—select station arms guard—ought obtain pillar-stone knights—such as Zhou Chang's sort.
s0441.idiomatic: After Your Majesty mounts the crane, when the great-grandson is still milk-teeth small, ring him with Zhou Chang granite—soldiers sworn to blunt any blade turned inward.

s0442.literal: Common custom shallow thin—knights lacking integrity modesty—Jia Mi little boy—relying favour reckless pride—yet shallow-middle weak-root followers—mutually inhale-learn—therefore generation titles Duke of Lu twenty-four Friends.
s0442.idiomatic: The age is vulgar, its men brittle; young Jia Mi struts on favor while shallow-root hangers-on imitate him—the world mocks them as Duke of Lu's twenty-four sworn companions.

s0443.literal: Further Mi formerly seeing Your servant memorial straighten heir-apparent—said: 'The Yan lad did boldly here—yet inspecting his intention—wishes with various Sima houses same.
s0443.idiomatic: When I petitioned for the heir, Mi once sneered—'Brave work for Yan's cub—but study his motive: he means to clasp hands with every Sima branch alive.'

s0444.idiomatic: —and my blood ran cold hearing it.

s0445.literal: Prostrate seeing edict pronounce brightness Man Fen, Yue Guang.
s0445.idiomatic: I applaud the edict that singles out Man Fen and Yue Guang for clarity.

s0446.literal: Attendant Gentleman Jia Yin—with Mi intimately related-by-marriage and managed—yet also kept estranged-distance—past after completing father's mourning—stopped home five years—although termed small setback—those with discernment esteemed him.
s0446.idiomatic: Attendant Gentleman Jia Yin was tethered to Mi by marriage brokerage yet edged away; five years mourning at home looked like setback and men of judgment prized him for it.

s0447.literal: Pan Yue, Miao Zheng et al. all Mi father's faction—mutually sink-float—literati-of-office shamed them—hearing his peace—none not deemed strange.
s0447.idiomatic: Pan Yue, Miao Zheng, and the rest floated in Jia Chong's faction; gentlemen held their nose at them yet marveled how lightly they ride the purge.

s0448.literal: Now edict book sudden-display their crimes—together all expelled sent out—commoners all say pure proper—Your servant alone call not.
s0448.idiomatic: The court now parades their guilt and casts them wholesale; the lanes cheer—yet Your servant disagrees.

s0449.literal: Only Pan Yue, Miao Zheng twenty-four persons—ought all uniformly dismissed—to stern wind-teaching.
s0449.idiomatic: Dismiss Pan Yue, Miao Zheng, and the entire score of twenty-four together—only that scours the lesson home.

s0450.literal: Court praised his loyalty fierce—promoted Hanzhong Governor.
s0450.idiomatic: The court praised his fearless loyalty and raised him governor of Hanzhong.

s0451.literal: Prince Zhao Lun died—already buried—Zuan thereby cart crushed his mound.
s0451.idiomatic: After Prince Zhao Sima Lun was buried, Zuan drove a wagon across his mound.

s0452.literal: At time Zhang Hua elder brother's son Jing afterward transferred Hanzhong—Zuan again memorial deemed ought return.
s0452.idiomatic: Later, when Zhang Hua's nephew Jing was shifted to Hanzhong, Zuan argued he belonged back at court.

s0453.literal: Zuan did not guard fine conduct—yet open-giving admired great cardinal-integrity.
s0453.idiomatic: Zuan shrugged at petty reputability but prized the grand virtues.

s0454.idiomatic: He died in office at fifty-nine.

s0455.literal: Zuan five sons—all open bright had talent-force.
s0455.idiomatic: His five sons were open-hearted men of parts.

s0456.literal: Eldest son Heng Liaoxi Governor—because Wang Jun self-employed his people—Heng unable attain office-assignment.
s0456.idiomatic: Eldest son Yan Heng was named to Liaoxi, yet Wang Jun planted his own men and barred Heng from ever taking command.

s0457.literal: Relied Qingzhou Inspector Gou Xi—punishments governance harsh brutal—Heng repeatedly incisive remonstrated—by Xi harmed killed.
s0457.idiomatic: He took refuge with Qingzhou inspector Gou Xi, whose rule was savage; Heng rebuked him again and again until Gou murdered him.

s0458.literal: Historian-courtiers say: Minhuai's deposition—Under Heaven titled his wrong.
s0458.idiomatic: The historians write: when Minhuai fell, the realm called it murder by edict.

s0459.literal: Yet all feared chaos-government's three-clan extirpation—cowed wanton-favorite's fierce cruel—thereupon caused planning ministers cherish loyalty yet tie tongue—righteous knights store fury yet swallow voice.
s0459.idiomatic: Yet terror of junta butchery and the favorite's knives sealed every planner's mouth and turned every honest man's shout inward.

s0460.literal: Yan Xubo's office already slight compared Gentleman-in-Attendance—rank not ascend compared halberdier—light life weight righteousness—view death like return—prostrate memorial awaiting stern execution—cart coffin toward cauldron-cleaver—inspect speech observe action—surely not loyalty straight grandeur!
s0460.idiomatic: Yan Zuan, style Xubo, sat lower than a palace gentleman and never rose to halberdier rank—yet he weighed righteousness above breath, rolled his coffin toward the cooking cauldron, and lay prone awaiting the blade: read his words, watch his deeds—was that not stalwart loyalty?

s0461.literal: Turning-glance Jin court dukes ministers—not once obtained compare their thrall-stable teeth-ranked.
s0461.idiomatic: Beside him the gilt ministers of Jin hardly rated beside his carriage lackeys.

s0462.literal: Maobo pure-to-end—wept Wang Jing thereby complete integrity.
s0462.idiomatic: Maobo finished as he lived—mourning Wang Jing to seal his honor.

s0463.literal: Xiuran chasing far-off justice—straightened Deng Ai thereby complete fame.
s0463.idiomatic: Xiuran prosecuted a dead man's case until Deng Ai was posthumously cleared—that was how he earned fame.

s0464.literal: Therefore obtained righteousness stirred bright age—grace flowed withered bones.
s0464.idiomatic: Their justice lit the dynasty and spilled mercy even on mouldering bones.

s0465.literal: Although Zhu Bo pursued discuss Xinxi-Hou—Luan Bu memorialized affair King Peng—not reach surpass those.
s0465.idiomatic: Zhu Bo's plea for the Marquis of Xinxi after Ma Yuan's fall and Luan Bu's memorial pleading for King Peng of Liang before Gaozu still do not surpass them.

s0466.literal: Eulogy says: touched righteousness collecting Hui—pure-end straightening Ai.
s0466.idiomatic: The verdict sings: Moved by principle, Xiang assembled Zhong Hui's bones; steadfast to the grave, Duan vindicated Deng Ai.

s0467.literal: Way already mutually equal—name also together great.
s0467.idiomatic: Their paths marched in step—their reputations loom together.

s0468.idiomatic: Lowly Xubo shouldered his bier yet schooled the throne.

s0469.literal: Pressed by these corrupting favorites—did not fulfil good scheme.
s0469.idiomatic: Vicious favorites boxed him round—sound counsel never ripened.

s0470.idiomatic: He ends like the ode—'they sip their tears; why sigh when it is too late?'
